---
title: "VILMA2"
subtitle: "A fast, open-source, time-domain spectral–finite-element solid-Earth model"
toc: false
---

**VILMA2** is a fast, open-source 3D solid-Earth model: a
self-gravitating, incompressible, Maxwell-viscoelastic sphere coupled to a
self-consistent **sea-level equation** with migrating coastlines. It is
designed as an open-source alternative to VILMA1 inside the
[CLIMBER-X](https://doi.org/10.5194/gmd-15-5905-2022) Earth system model
[@Willeit2022], and more generally as a reusable glacial isostatic adjustment
(GIA) engine for ice-sheet and sea-level work.

The numerical method follows the **spectral–finite-element, time-domain**
approach of @Martinec2000: spherical harmonics horizontally, finite elements
radially, and an explicit memory-stress integration of the Maxwell rheology in
time. The solver is **3D-ready from the start**: laterally varying viscosity
uses the same per-degree solve as the 1-D model. It is validated against the
published GIA community benchmarks [@Spada2011; @Martinec2018;
@Weerdesteijn2023]. VILMA2 is free software under the GNU General Public
License v3.0.

## Why this method

The structural advantage of this approach is that, with an **explicit**
Maxwell time scheme, the stiffness solve has **no angular coupling**. Each
spherical-harmonic degree $\ell$ decouples into an independent, small, banded
radial system. This makes the solver embarrassingly parallel and cheap.
Lateral (3D) viscosity never couples the harmonics in the solve. It enters only
through the explicitly known memory stress, which is evaluated pointwise on the
Gauss–Legendre grid and transformed back to spectral space each step (a
pseudo-spectral treatment). Its cost lies in these transforms of the memory
advance, which dominate the run time of a 3-D run. The **1D and 3D code
paths are therefore the same solver**.

| Method family | Examples | 3D viscosity | Speed | Fit for purpose |
|---|---|:---:|:---:|---|
| Normal-mode + Love numbers + SLE | SELEN, TABOO, ALMA3 | no (1D only) | fast (1D) | dead end for 3D |
| **Time-domain spectral–FE** | **VILMA1** [@Martinec2000] | **yes** | **fast** | **chosen** |
| Full 3D FE/FV | CitcomSVE, ASPECT, Elmer | yes | slow, heavy | too complex |

## Status

VILMA2 is validated against the published GIA benchmarks and is starting to be
used for science. It is versioned 0.x, so the namelist and the host API may
still change. The implemented model comprises the spectral–finite-element
solver, the viscoelastic time stepping, the self-consistent sea-level equation
with migrating coastlines, rotational feedback, laterally varying (3-D)
viscosity, restart and spin-up, online remapping of lon-lat forcing, and a
host-coupling API.

Each benchmark is an executable test with a pass/fail exit. The table gives the
tolerance each test asserts and the difference measured with the reference
build (ifx `-Ofast` on the AWI cluster albedo).

| Benchmark | Asserted | Measured |
|---|---|---|
| [Love numbers](benchmarks/love-numbers.qmd), M3–L70–V01 [@Spada2011] | 1 % (elastic $h$, $k$ at degrees 2–48; fluid at 2–8) | $h$ ≤ 0.08 % to degree 256; $k$, $\ell$ exceed 1 % above degrees 96, 144 |
| [Disc load](benchmarks/disc.qmd) [@Spada2011] | 6 % / 4 % of peak (elastic $u$ / $N$); 3 % (center uplift, 1–10 kyr) | 4.0 % / 2.8 %; ≤ 0.6 % |
| [Cap load, case A](benchmarks/sea-level.qmd) [@Martinec2018] | 1.5 % ($u$, horizontal), 3 % (geoid) | 0.5 %, 0.7 %, 1.9 % |
| [Sea-level equation](benchmarks/sea-level.qmd), C2/D3/E2/F1 [@Martinec2018] | 8–35 % of peak, by field | D3, E2, F1 ≤ 7.6 %, rsl ≤ 1.8 %; C2 up to 28 % |
| [Polar motion](benchmarks/rotation.qmd), Spada test 3/2 [@Spada2011] | 3 % | ≤ 0.9 % |
| [Low-viscosity zone](benchmarks/lvz.qmd) [@Weerdesteijn2023] | 8 % | 2.6 %, 1.0 % |

The model builds and passes its test suite with ifx on albedo and with gfortran
on macOS and Ubuntu (GitHub CI). It builds with ifx on DKRZ levante.

What is still open:

- **Sea-level case C2.** A uniform 5.9 m offset in sea surface and a degree-1
  pattern of about 7 m in uplift, not yet attributed. The other three cases
  agree to below 1 m.
- **The 3-D viscosity path** is compared with other codes only in the
  axisymmetric low-viscosity-zone case (200 yr) and with VILMA1 on the last
  deglaciation. No multi-code benchmark of a realistic 3-D structure at glacial
  time scales exists yet.
- **Toroidal flow** driven by lateral viscosity is **on by default**
  (`l_toroidal = .true.`). In the 3-D last deglaciation it changes relative sea
  level by 2–3 m rms and up to 92 m near the former ice sheets.
  `l_toroidal = .false.` makes 3-D runs 1.5–1.8 times faster, for quick runs
  that do not depend on local sea level ([Toroidal flow](physics/toroidal.qmd)).
- **Rotation coupled to the sea-level equation** has no published benchmark
  and is checked for consistency only.

See the [benchmarks](benchmarks/index.qmd) for the full validation ladder.
